subject.title: [Feature]: Allow restoring rejected skill workshop proposals back to pending

question: Should Skill Workshop support restoring rejected proposals back to pending as a core lifecycle action, and what audit/history semantics should that restore preserve?
rationale: This changes the proposal state machine and public CLI/Gateway/UI surface; the code path is clear, but whether rejected proposals are reversible and how rejection history remains visible is a product decision.

options.title: Accept a narrow restore lifecycle
options.body: Review the linked PR or a replacement that only allows rejected-to-pending, preserves workspace scoping and locking, and records enough history for operators.

options.title: Keep rejection terminal
options.body: Reject the feature direction and close the linked PR if maintainers want rejected proposals to remain immutable review history.

options.title: Defer pending audit model
options.body: Keep the issue open but ask for an audit/history design before accepting any public restore command or RPC.

recommendation.title: Accept a narrow restore lifecycle
recommendation.body: Review the linked PR or a replacement that only allows rejected-to-pending, preserves workspace scoping and locking, and records enough history for operators.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current Skill Workshop proposal lifecycle and are the strongest history-backed owner for the state-machine direction.
